teaching.hint: Which task frequencies can force idle gaps even when other tasks are freely reordered?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The highest frequency dictates the number of cooldown-sized frames; ties occupy distinct positions in the final frame.
solution_outline.approach: Count tasks per label. Let f be the maximum frequency and t the number of labels with that frequency. Compare the task count with the frame bound `(f-1)(n+1)+t` and take the larger.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The frame bound accounts for f repetitions of every most frequent label while reserving at least n intervening slots between equal labels.
solution_outline.correctness: The task count N and frame expression (f-1)(n+1)+t are lower bounds. Arrange the f highest-frequency occurrences in f layers separated by n slots, placing tied labels alongside them. Other labels fill the slots without violating their own spacing. When they outnumber vacant slots, the layers expand so all N tasks run without idle; otherwise the frame expression is attained.
solution_outline.complexity: O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space because the alphabet has 26 labels.
solution_outline.pitfall: Using only one most frequent label in the final frame undercounts when several labels tie at frequency f.

common_wrong_turns: Always insert n idle slots between same-label tasks
source_fidelity_notes: The intervening-interval meaning, optional idle, reorder permission, and n=0 boundary are explicit.
